AgentQuestion.label: Checking can settle it
AgentQuestion.explain: An open question an agent can settle by reading, running or testing.

BrianQuestion.label: Brian's call
BrianQuestion.explain: A product or priority question; it carries a recommendation and a default.

Concept.label: Concept
Concept.explain: A domain-model concept; open the Domain model tab for its definition.

nodes.explain: Blocks: S4: Q45 retires a check when its incident's saved world is refused by a declared law; with laws left out that test can pass on worlds that still have the bug. Also A1 and A4, whose expected results include a payment law..

nodes.label: Q50: What counts as finished
nodes.explain: Blocks: Whether the paid builds in S5, L5, A4 and A6 run now, and which defect is fixed next. Merges under the plan stay ungated by Brian's review; only new paid builds wait..

nodes.label: Q51: Live network with no lines
nodes.explain: Blocks: Whether the Network view can be trusted in a live run; issue #316..

nodes.label: Q52: Does the person asked respond

nodes.label: Q56: A rule that writes less than it declared
nodes.explain: Blocks: Whether a world's declared write scopes can be read as what its rules actually maintain; a generated rule that silently stops updating a field it owns goes unnoticed..

nodes.label: Q57: String fields have no declared values

nodes.label: Q58: Promises beyond support (a Commitment kind)

nodes.label: Q59: Does the people path transfer to a different situation

nodes.label: Q60: Act on the Waltzman lineage review

nodes.label: Q61: Outside vocabularies never evaluated

nodes.label: Q62: Meaning coverage beyond the six bound moves

nodes.label: Q63: A non-authoritative estimate as a rule input

nodes.label: Q64: Meaning is looked up by bare move name

nodes.explain: Blocks: Whether the status check is evidence about read scopes or only about the spec's text; Q34..

nodes.label: Q67: Write-path placeholders bind to any participant

nodes.label: Q68: No lockfile; donor check needs a missing checkout
nodes.explain: Blocks: Reproducing a run's exact dependencies, and running the donor check at all..

nodes.label: Q69: Hardening: law identity, discovery cap, mechanic errors

nodes.label: Q70: A hosted CI workflow against the local-checks rule
nodes.explain: Blocks: Whether the repository keeps a hosted check beside its local one; nothing merges on it today..

nodes.explain: Blocks: J1's record shape (whole report or a summary of it) and A2 on large worlds..

nodes.label: Q75: Constraint question or someone's choice
nodes.explain: Blocks: J2's routing step and A5 (Rosa's own resident decides accept or refuse)..

nodes.label: Q76: How to write norms and credential holders
nodes.explain: Blocks: J4's design and A6 (the password fixture: Mallory phishes Alice's password, is logged in, and the breach has consequences only after an observer acts)..

nodes.label: Affordance (offered move)
nodes.explain: A move the rules say a person can try now, with its open fields; the page a decider picks from or an attempt is read against.

nodes.label: Agenda count
nodes.explain: group_decision.agenda_items: a bare number of matters put before the decision; an item has no content. Declared in the group-decision component and changed by the compiled put-matter-on-agenda and settle-agenda-matter rules.

nodes.label: Attempt (in own words)
nodes.explain: What a resident says it physically tries, in its own words, with no outcome field: the world, not the speaker, decides what happens.

nodes.label: Attempt reading
nodes.explain: The interpreter's typed reading of an attempt: one move kind and its field rows (field, value, quoted_span: the words in the attempt behind that value), or the kind 'wait'; read as unmatched if it names an unknown kind or entity, misses a field, or quotes words not said.

nodes.label: Build
nodes.explain: Description to spec, actions, rules, assembly, scripted test run and score.

nodes.label: World Builder and its bundle
nodes.explain: The public page and service where a person describes a world, approves its rules and watches it run; a build's output is an authoring bundle.

nodes.label: Hard causal parent
nodes.explain: An earlier event a rule declares as mechanically supporting this one; kept apart from the information a person merely had in mind.

nodes.label: Causal trace
nodes.explain: The retained chain of events of a run, each naming the move or process, its checks and its changes; the evidence for any claim about a run.

nodes.label: Check
nodes.explain: One condition on a move or process (actual versus required); a move commits only when every check holds, else the event records which failed.

nodes.label: Compiler
nodes.explain: Turns proposed rules into installed rules and derives what each may read and write.

nodes.label: Concern
nodes.explain: An objection a group holds on a delivered item: open, under remedy or resolved, with answered and remedy_by.

nodes.label: Consequence report
nodes.explain: Plan ai-judge J1 (planned, not implemented): every knock-on effect and blocker the engine works out for one attempt, as one record the judge and the run page read.

nodes.label: Credential holder
nodes.explain: Plan ai-judge J4 (planned, not implemented): who holds a credential (a password, a signed release) as a fact in the world that can change: told, overheard, copied, forged or phished. The mechanism checks the credential, not the holder.

nodes.label: Engine
nodes.explain: Applies each attempt atomically or refuses it with a recorded reason; runs due processes each tick.

nodes.label: Entity and component
nodes.explain: An entity is one thing in the world (person, wall, glass, decision) with an id, a label, categories and typed components; a component is a named record of typed fields (boundary.passable, group_decision.status) that checks read and effects write.

nodes.label: Event
nodes.explain: The record of one attempt or process step: status, checks, changes, an id like r14-e00012.

nodes.label: Generated actions and rules
nodes.explain: The moves and processes the fixed parts do not cover, written by the rules-writing AI and compiled.

nodes.label: Group decision
nodes.explain: A decision with support, deadline, deployment and review; changed only by fixed rules.

nodes.label: Build in an agent harness
nodes.explain: Decision 008: worlds built by an agent that drafts, checks and edits; scripts/world_harness.py exists but the live service does not call it.

nodes.label: Judge ruling
nodes.explain: Plan ai-judge J2 (planned, not implemented): Concordia's game master (EventResolution), given the consequence report, rules on the constraint an unmatched attempt raises (can coins change hands here?), as a proposed rule, never an outcome or another person's choice.

nodes.label: Law check
nodes.explain: Plan declared-laws S2 (built): inside the same commit as the write-scope check, every move, round process and knock-on effect is checked against the world's declared laws; a breach refuses the whole step or moment as law_breach and names the law, and nothing changes. A test-run breach is a build finding sent to the rules writer and the world designer.

nodes.label: Executable-law fingerprint
nodes.explain: Roadmap hardening item: fingerprint the exact executable law and compiler version.

nodes.label: Installed mechanic
nodes.explain: One installed action rule: an action kind's selector, checks, effects and derived reads and writes, compiled and frozen in the profile; the root rule says installed mechanics alone decide what happens.

nodes.label: Mechanisms library
nodes.explain: Reusable hand-written rule families (liquid, ownership, thermal, damage, time) that reference worlds such as Castaway register (reference_worlds/castaway/overheat.py:14); generated worlds get only their compiled mechanics and processes (scripts/run_authored_world.py:71, Q28).

nodes.label: Norm
nodes.explain: Plan ai-judge J4 (planned, not implemented): what people expect or forbid (bribery is illegal; only Alice should log in). It can be broken; a breach is recorded and has consequences only when someone notices and acts. Never written as a declared law.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.explain: What one actor sees this round: the fields its senses and position allow, never the whole world.

nodes.label: People world
nodes.explain: A world built from a description about people: people, information, moments and the fixed people rules.

nodes.label: Person and brief
nodes.explain: A person the spec names, with goals and beliefs, and the brief only their own resident reads.

nodes.label: Place and way
nodes.explain: Where things are, and what lies between two places (a door, a brick wall) with whether it is passable; written per world as entities from the bundle contract, and the move rule checks the way.

nodes.label: Frozen mechanic profile
nodes.explain: The validated, installed rules of a world, frozen under one id before any run; changing a rule means a new profile.

nodes.label: Readout
nodes.explain: One AI summary of a run whose every cited event id is checked against the run.

nodes.label: Remedy
nodes.explain: A fix of a concern that takes 2 rounds; it can be stopped part-way by the concern's holder objecting.

nodes.label: Resident
nodes.explain: One Concordia AI agent per person: sees its brief, memory and what it can see, and answers belief, attempt (in its own words), expected effect and work; the older menu reply picks an offered move.

nodes.label: Rules retry
nodes.explain: A second rules attempt after a rejection or weak score; skipped after 80 s.

nodes.label: Independent rules review
nodes.explain: Plan declared-laws S3 (built): a separate model call with a fresh context reads the description, the declared laws and the written rules, and lists concrete mismatches (each naming a rule and the words it contradicts) for the rules writer to fix; findings, never a pass mark. Runs on things worlds and, from 2026-10-30, on people worlds.

nodes.label: Run loop
nodes.explain: Each round: everyone decides, picks are submitted in a rotating order, then processes run.

nodes.label: Scene replay
nodes.explain: The page's round-by-round picture of a run: who did what and said what, rebuilt from the run rows; it already quotes a retry's own words.

nodes.label: Linguistic Core sense and roles
nodes.explain: The meaning and participant roles of a move kind, supplied by Linguistic Core; never its effects, quantities or timing.

nodes.label: Share link and replay
nodes.explain: A saved run rebuilt from the run log that a visitor replays with no AI calls.

nodes.label: Skill roll
nodes.explain: Plan S3: a move's outcome depends on a seeded, recorded roll against the person's skill, so someone untrained who flies a helicopter can crash it.

nodes.label: Support
nodes.explain: A member's stance on the decision: none, full or conditional on a concern.

nodes.label: Task
nodes.explain: A watched field value that takes several rounds, started by a person or the world, ended by a process: finished or failed part-way.

nodes.label: Scripted test run
nodes.explain: The build's free run with simple moves that scores the rules and lists long tasks and whether each can fail part-way.

nodes.label: Unmatched attempt
nodes.explain: An attempt no move kind covers: it changes nothing, the person learns nothing came of it, and the run lists it for the rules writer.

nodes.label: Waltzman reference components
nodes.explain: Trust, risk, readiness and commitment components and analyses of the hand-written Waltzman world.

nodes.label: World design (bundle)
nodes.explain: The build's first AI step: it reads the description and writes the world's people, places, things and starting state as an authoring bundle; plan declared-laws S1 adds the world's resources and laws to its output, and the rules writer receives them as input.

nodes.label: Declared world law
nodes.explain: Plan declared-laws S1 (built): a law the AI writes when it designs a world, in that world's own terms: a resource whose total only named moves may change (pencils are made only by the factory's make move), or a move meaning such as 'a purchase moves goods one way and payment the other'. Never a fixed list of move types. The bundle validator checks each law's shape; the rules writer is given the laws and told to keep them; the engine keeps them at every commit (S2, built).

nodes.label: Declared write scope
nodes.explain: The fields a rule says it may change; the Engine refuses any change outside them. Read scopes are recorded, not enforced.
